g.text: partition_checkpoints backs the merge barrier; top_k_results is the only table a reader ever queries
(N rows per run -- one per partition)
(1 row per run -- NEVER scales with log size)
THE TABLE THAT DOESN'T EXIST: visitor_counts
One row per distinct visitor ID would reintroduce the ~10GB, cardinality-scaling problem
this design exists to avoid (Module 00) -- so it is never materialized, anywhere.
The only per-visitor rows anywhere in this schema live inside results_json (<= K rows)
and local_top_k_json (<= C x K rows per partition) -- both fixed, small multiples of K.
